tagline: Around Minneapolis at 25 miles an hour, on red asphalt.
intro: The parkways go round Minneapolis at 25 miles an hour, on asphalt tinted red so a driver can tell which way to turn. From the old milling district at Saint Anthony Falls the route goes down the Mississippi gorge to Minnehaha Park, follows Minnehaha Creek west to the Chain of Lakes, and turns north through Theodore Wirth Park and along Victory Memorial Drive before crossing the river into Northeast.

Horace Cleveland drew the first of it in the 1880s, for a city that bought the shores of its lakes before anyone could build on them. It is still not quite a ring. A missing link between the river and Northeast keeps it open.

moments.title: Stone Arch Bridge
moments.text: James J. Hill's railroad bridge of 1883, called Hill's Folly for a time, is the only stone arch bridge on the whole Mississippi and now carries walkers and bicycles.

moments.title: Minnehaha Falls
moments.text: Longfellow made the falls famous in The Song of Hiawatha without ever coming to see them; the park around them was Cleveland's design.

moments.title: Lake of the Isles
moments.text: Dredged into shape in the 1880s, the lake kept two of its four islands, still in virgin woods, where landing is forbidden.

practical: Heavy vehicles such as semi-trailer trucks and buses are largely banned from the parkways.
